dt5_the_asymmetry.topic: State action, corporate speech in both directions: Halleck, Citizens United, Moody v. NetChoice, Montana I-194, Democracy for All

claims.text: Halleck, 17 June 2019, 5-4 (Kavanaugh; Sotomayor dissent with Ginsburg, Breyer, Kagan): 'the Free Speech Clause prohibits only governmental abridgment of speech'; 'merely hosting speech by others is not a traditional, exclusive public function'; MNN, a private nonprofit designated by NYC to run Manhattan public-access channels, was not a state actor. Dissent: 'a case about principals and agents'

Moody v. NetChoice, 1 July 2024: judgments vacated and remanded 9-0; Kagan's opinion joined in full by Roberts, Sotomayor, Kavanaugh, Barrett, Jackson in part; Thomas and Alito (with Thomas, Gorsuch) concurred only in the judgment; challenged Florida and Texas 2021 laws
Moody majority: government violates platforms' rights when it 'interferes with such editorial choices'; disagreeing with 'the mix of speech' is 'not [a] valid, let alone substantial' interest

Citizens United, 21 Jan 2010: 5-4 (Kennedy, Roberts, Scalia, Alito, Thomas) struck the ban on corporate and union independent expenditures; Stevens, Ginsburg, Breyer, Sotomayor dissented; arose from Hillary: The Movie; Thomas alone would have struck the disclosure provisions
Citizens United disclosure holding: 'the vote was 8-1 in favor of a disclosure law also challenged by the plaintiffs'

Pew March 2026: 33% correctly say the Constitution does not protect the press from interference by private companies (R 32%, D 36%); 60% correctly say it is legal for platforms to restrict content (R 61%, D 62%)

Pew Feb 2024: 83% say platforms likely intentionally censor political viewpoints (R 93%, D 74%); 44% say tech companies favor liberal views, 15% conservative, 37% equal; 51% want more regulation (D 60%, R 45%)

Meta launched the American Technology Excellence Project, a super PAC of 'tens of millions' of dollars, on 23 Sept 2025 to oppose state AI regulation and back tech-friendly candidates of both parties; a California PAC followed in Aug 2025
Trump's 2025 inaugural committee raised a record $239M per FEC filing; Amazon, Meta and JPMorgan Chase gave at least $1M each; Sam Altman gave $1M personally

dt5_what_was_moderated.topic: Documented moderation in every direction: Palestine-related content (HRW, BSR, Oversight Board, Meta Zionist policy, X, TikTok) and the laptop story, Trump suspension, Meta 2025 shift

claims.text: HRW reviewed 1,050 verified cases (from 1,285 reports received by 28 Nov 2023) from 60+ countries, Oct-Nov 2023: 1,049 peaceful pro-Palestine content, 1 pro-Israel; six patterns incl. removals, suspensions, feature limits, 'shadow banning'; cases self-reported via a call for evidence; HRW says the report 'is not a global comparative analysis of overall censorship'

Meta on the HRW report: 'the implication that we deliberately and systemically suppress a particular voice is false'; said the report 'ignores the realities of enforcing our policies globally during a fast-moving, highly polarized and intense conflict'

BSR (commissioned by Meta), released 22 Sept 2022, on 10-21 May 2021: 'adverse human rights impact' on Palestinian users' expression; over-enforcement on Palestinian content and under-enforcement on violating content; Arabic hostile-speech classifier with no Hebrew equivalent; too few Arabic and Hebrew reviewers; US terrorist designations with 'disproportionate focus' on Muslim-identified groups; Meta: 10 recommendations implemented, 4 partly, 6 assessing, 1 declined

Oversight Board, March 2024: blanket treatment of 'shaheed' 'substantially and disproportionately restricts free expression'; Meta said the word likely 'accounts for more content removals ... than any other single word or phrase'; July 2024 Meta lifted the blanket ban, removing it only with 'signals of violence'

Oversight Board, 4 Sept 2024, three cases: 'from the river to the sea' posts left up; the phrase 'has multiple meanings'; decision by a majority; ADL and World Jewish Congress 'disappointed', call the phrase 'inherently genocidal and anti-Semitic'

Meta July 2024: removes attacks on 'Zionists' used as a proxy for Jews or Israelis (dehumanization, claims Zionists control the world or media); rule applies when the term is not 'explicitly about the political movement'; Meta: 'nothing approaching a global consensus' on the term; consulted 145 stakeholders
Musk, 18 Nov 2023: ''decolonization,' 'from the river to the sea' and similar euphemisms necessarily imply genocide'; clear calls for extreme violence lead to suspension on X

TikTok USDS joint venture finalised about 22 Jan 2026: Oracle, Silver Lake, MGX and others 80.1%, ByteDance 19.9%; Adam Presser CEO; a May video of Presser said TikTok had tweaked its 'Zionist' policy so using it to demean is hate speech; concerns about Palestine content raised but no new policy announced with the deal
Twitter blocked the NY Post Hunter Biden story on 14 Oct 2020; Dorsey 15 Oct: 'Straight blocking of URLs was wrong, and we updated our policy to fix'; hacked-materials policy changed to allow labels

Zuckerberg to Jordan (posted 26 Aug 2024): Biden administration 'repeatedly pressured our teams for months to censor certain COVID-19 content, including humor and satire'; 'I believe the government pressure was wrong'; on the laptop story, 'in retrospect, we shouldn't have demoted the story'; Meta took responsibility for final decisions

Oversight Board, 5 May 2021: Trump's suspension 'justified' but the indefinite penalty 'indeterminate and standardless'; Twitter permanently suspended Trump on 8 Jan 2021 citing 'the risk of further incitement of violence'
Meta, 7 Jan 2025: ended US third-party fact-checking for Community Notes; said its systems had 'gone too far'; Zuckerberg: elections a 'cultural tipping point towards once again prioritizing speech'

dt5_government_pressure_and_the_way_back.topic: Government pressure on platforms and broadcasters under both administrations; routes to undo Citizens United

claims.text: NRA v. Vullo, 30 May 2024, unanimous (Sotomayor): Vullo, head of New York's Department of Financial Services, was 'free to criticize the NRA' but could not 'threaten enforcement actions' against regulated entities 'to punish or suppress the NRA's gun-promotion advocacy'; Bantam Books (1963) framework; case reinstated

EO 14149, 20 Jan 2025: no federal officer 'engages in or facilitates any conduct that would unconstitutionally abridge the free speech'; AG 'shall investigate the activities of the Federal Government over the last 4 years'

White House response to Zuckerberg (Aug 2024): 'When confronted with a deadly pandemic, this Administration encouraged responsible actions to protect public health and safety'; tech companies should make 'independent choices about the information they present'

Kimmel: monologue 15 Sept 2025; FCC chair Carr 17 Sept: 'We can do this the easy way or the hard way'; Nexstar and Sinclair pulled the show; ABC suspended it 17 Sept; returned 23 Sept; Nexstar's $6.2bn Tegna deal pending before the FCC; Cruz: 'right out of Goodfellas'; Rand Paul critical; Carr: Disney 'made the business decision'; Carr questioned by Senate Commerce Dec 2025 and a House E&C subcommittee Jan 2026

FCC approved Paramount-Skydance 24 July 2025 with a CBS News ombudsman for at least two years and no DEI programs; followed Paramount's $16M settlement of Trump's '60 Minutes' suit; Carr: 'It is time for a change'; Commissioner Gomez dissented ('cannot support this order')
S.J.Res.19 (Democracy for All) cloture failed 54-42 on 11 Sept 2014

Democracy for All Amendment reintroduced by Sen. Shaheen, press release 28 March 2025, with about 40 Democratic and independent cosponsors; would let Congress and the states set campaign finance rules and limit corporate spending

Montana I-194 (statute) qualified for the Nov 2026 ballot on 17 Aug 2026: limits artificial persons' powers, bars spending on candidate elections, parties and ballot issues, forfeiture of business privileges; news exempt; CI-135 approved for signatures 30 Apr 2026, not listed as qualified

I-194: Transparent Election Initiative submitted ~50,000 signatures 16 June 2026 (30,121 needed); Montana Chamber: 'I-194 would prohibit Montana businesses and nonprofits from participating in the political process'; Montana voters' 2012 I-166 corporate ban was overturned in 2013

Article V: Congress proposes amendments 'whenever two thirds of both Houses shall deem it necessary', or a convention on application of two-thirds of state legislatures; ratification 'by the Legislatures of three fourths of the several States' (or conventions)
